summary.headline: ASK Automotive Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 47.5% to a record, with EBITDA of INR185 crores (+30%) and PAT of INR102 crores (+27.3%).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 set quarterly records for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, the 12th consecutive quarter of robust performance since listing. Excluding alloy pass-through (23 pp) and the wheel assembly reduction (5 pp), net revenue grew 29.5% YoY against industry two-wheeler production growth of 16.5%. EBITDA margin was 11.8% reported, depressed by pass-through aluminium prices; management says it would be about 13.5% or a little more on an adjusted basis. In H1 FY27, consolidated revenue grew 49.6% (net 27.6%), EBITDA rose 31.3% to INR348 crores and PAT rose 28% to INR187 crores. The HPDC alloy wheel supply to a Japanese OEM began on 3 August 2026, and the second captive solar plant (11.55 MW, Bikaner) was operationalised in October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Growth 47.5% YoY (net of alloy pass-through and wheel assembly reduction: 29.5%)
Growth 49.6% YoY (net of pass-through and wheel reduction: 27.6%)

segments.name: Advanced braking systems
segments.commentary: Revenue up 46% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 47% YoY in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Aluminium lightweighting precision solutions (ALPS)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 69% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 72% in H1 FY27; passenger vehicle revenue grew 79% in Q2 and 67% in H1. EV revenue grew 98% YoY in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Safety control cables
segments.commentary: Revenue up 33% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 27% in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Roughly 11% of overall revenue; management says it grows faster than the brake segment, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects net revenue growth of high teens in FY27 despite a higher post-GST 2.0 base in Q3 and Q4.
Export guidance was INR145 crores; management now says it will touch INR180 crores and is confident of exceeding it. An analyst asked about crossing INR200 crores; no explicit answer was given.
Alloy wheel revenue from the Japanese customer is expected at about INR80 crores in FY27 and up to INR240 crores in FY28.
Capex budgeted at INR700 crores for FY27 and about INR500 crores for FY28; the 20th plant (fourth Bangalore plant) is due around 14-15 January 2027.
EBITDA margins are expected to stay at or slightly improve on the current level if aluminium prices remain high; management expects the margin trajectory not to fall in H2 FY27.
Management sees the industry growing about 10% over the medium term and EV reaching about 20% of two-wheeler market in about two to three years.
Exports expected to grow more than 25% YoY on average; FY28 export growth guidance to be given next quarter.
capex_capacity: 19th plant (friction material expansion for brakes) commissioned.
20th plant (fourth Bangalore plant) expected around 14-15 January 2027, serving southern customers.
The earlier Bangalore plant (about INR380 crores investment) is running at about 90% capacity utilisation.
Second captive solar plant of 11.55 MW at Bikaner, Rajasthan, operationalised October 2026.
Capex has averaged at least INR500 crores a year for the last four years, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Alloy price (aluminium) increases are passed through to revenue; this inflates revenue and dilutes margin percentages (denominator effect), per management.

HPDC alloy wheel regular supply began 3 August 2026 to a Japanese OEM under a technical collaboration with Kyushu Yanagawa, Japan; described as the first HPDC alloy wheels in Indian two-wheelers. Other Indian OEM approvals are in final safety testing, with supply expected next FY.
Honda is about 35% of total revenue; management says content per vehicle is slightly higher with Honda.
EV kit value is about INR1,250-1,300 versus about INR950 for ICE (about 1.3-1.4x). Ola is weaker; new EV customers include Ather, TVS, Hero and a smaller Bajaj share.
Trade receivables rose in H1 due to higher sales and higher aluminium prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the high-teens full-year growth guidance on net revenue excluding alloy pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed the high-teens growth guidance refers to net revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will export run-rate of about INR100 crores in H1 continue in H2, and are there new export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of H2 but did not give a new order-win detail; it raised FY27 export guidance from INR145 crores to INR180 crores and expects to cross it.

qa_highlights.question: Alloy wheel ramp-up and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 supply of about INR80 crores from the Japanese customer, rising to INR240 crores in FY28; alloy wheel EBITDA margins are expected to be in line with company margins.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: INR700 crores budgeted for FY27 (could slip into FY28 if machines arrive late) and about INR500 crores in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and repayment plan given capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is funded from internal accruals; debt-equity is about 0.5x and debt-to-EBITDA is kept near one year of EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Adjusted margin excluding aluminium impact versus 13-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says adjusted margin would be about 13.5% or a little more in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for higher other expenses in Q1 and Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly contractual labour charges, which rose with a sharp increase in minimum wages in Haryana and other states (management cited about 35%).

risks_watch: Aluminium price volatility: it inflates revenue, depresses reported margins, and drives receivables higher.
High base from GST 2.0 effects in Q3 and Q4 FY27; analysts expect slower H2 growth.
Export guidance and the INR200 crore target depend on geopolitical conditions, per management.
Customer concentration: Honda about 35% of revenue; Japanese OEM is the sole HPDC alloy wheel customer so far.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage increases in Haryana and other states.
Capex timing: the FY27 INR700 crore budget could shift to FY28 if machine deliveries slip.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, capex and FY28, with several forward-looking claims. Cautious and evasive on specifics: export FY28 guidance was deferred, the Indian OEM alloy wheel timing is open, and the margin question was answered by pointing to absolute EBITDA growth.
key_quotes: Happy to share that we have achieved highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
EBITDA margin percentage appears lower due to pass-through alloy prices.
Volatility in alloy prices may affect margin percentages due to the denominator effect. However, in absolute terms, our EBITDA growth is in line with the net revenue growth.
So EBITDA margins will remain in sync with the company's EBITDA margins.
The margin trajectory will be the same if the aluminium prices remain high like this.
